Compute Overview

1. What is the Compute Grid?
  • The Compute Grid allows you to execute arbitrary code on cluster nodes — closures, callables, runnables, and custom tasks;
  • Instead of moving data to the application, you move the computation to where the data lives;
  • Ignite handles distribution, load balancing, and failover automatically;
2. Why use Distributed Compute?
  • Data locality — execute computations on nodes that hold the relevant data, eliminating network transfer;
  • Parallelism — distribute work across all nodes for faster execution;
  • Failover — if a node fails during computation, Ignite can retry on another node;
3. Executing IgniteRunnable
  • Fire-and-forget execution with no return value: 
    // Run on a random node
ignite.compute().run(() -> {
    System.out.println("Hello from " + Ignition.localIgnite().name());
});

// Broadcast to ALL nodes
ignite.compute().broadcast(() -> {
    System.out.println("Hello from every node!");
});
4. Executing IgniteCallable
  • Execute tasks that return a value: 
    // Call on a random node
int result = ignite.compute().call(() -> {
    return Runtime.getRuntime().availableProcessors();
});

// Call on ALL nodes, collect results
Collection<Integer> cpuCounts = ignite.compute().broadcast(() -> {
    return Runtime.getRuntime().availableProcessors();
});

int totalCPUs = cpuCounts.stream().mapToInt(Integer::intValue).sum();
5. Map-Reduce with ComputeTask
  • For complex distributed computations, implement ComputeTask: 
    public class WordCountTask extends ComputeTaskSplitAdapter<String, Integer> {

    @Override
    protected Collection<? extends ComputeJob> split(int gridSize, String text) {
        // Split work into jobs — one per word
        String[] words = text.split(" ");
        List<ComputeJob> jobs = new ArrayList<>();
        for (String word : words) {
            jobs.add(new ComputeJobAdapter() {
                @Override public Object execute() {
                    return word.length();
                }
            });
        }
        return jobs;
    }

    @Override
    public Integer reduce(List<ComputeJobResult> results) {
        // Aggregate results from all jobs
        return results.stream()
            .mapToInt(r -> (int) r.getData())
            .sum();
    }
}

int totalLength = ignite.compute().execute(WordCountTask.class, "Hello World");
6. Async Execution
  • All compute methods have async counterparts: 
    IgniteFuture<Integer> future = ignite.compute().callAsync(() -> {
    return expensiveComputation();
});

future.listen(f -> System.out.println("Result: " + f.get()));
